column1: # ci-matrix.tsv — every REAL e2e suite, and how its client is provided.
# Columns: protocol <TAB> runner <TAB> direction <TAB> why <TAB> tools
#   protocol    the mount path AND the name in the e2e suite
#   runner      ubuntu-latest, or container:<image> for the distro managers
#   direction   which promise the SUITE tests - not what the protocol can do:
#                 hosted      the client PUBLISHES its own artefact and reads
#                             it back. Used when the adapter has a write path.
#                 pull-only   the client FETCHES an upstream artefact. This says
#                             nothing about whether the protocol COULD be
#                             published to; where the reason is "the adapter has
#                             no write path", the `why` column says so.
#                 build-only  reserved for a target that can only be built
#   why         the human explanation, including why a protocol is pull-only
#   tools       the easysetup setups the suite needs (space separated)
# A protocol was marked pull-only purely because its suite had not been extended
# yet: conan and pub both have full write paths (AuthorizeWriteScoped, and conan
# advertises upload_zip in its capabilities). The direction column describes the
# SUITE, not the product - the same mistake as reading Kind: Mirror as "cannot
#   ubuntu-latest   the client comes from easysetup. ONE job per protocol.
#                   ONLY for the distro package managers. `apk` is Alpine's
#                   package manager and does not exist on Ubuntu; `apt`/`dnf` on
#                   Ubuntu would test THIS image's package handling against a
#                   foreign distro's repository, which is the wrong subject.
#                   These three genuinely require the userland they test.
# --- application-level clients: installed with actions on ubuntu-latest ---

column4: deno via denoland/setup-deno (JSR packages through npm.jsr.io, the npm protocol)
conan via pip (installed in the job)
Apache Ivy (jar fetched in the job) on actions/setup-java
jenkins-plugin-cli (jar fetched in the job) + setup-java

column1: # --- distro package managers: these NEED their own userland ---

column4: pacman via the archlinux image (no cross-distro substitute)
apt tests THIS distro's archive layout
dnf tests THIS distro's repomd metadata
